science.description: A new era of genome research began in 2012 with the discovery that CRISPR/Cas9 could function as molecular scissors to cut specific DNA sequences. Over time, scientists harnessed CRISPR as a genome-editing tool, which held the promise of precise gene removal and addition for research purposes, targeted therapies for genetic diseases like cystic fibrosis or Huntington's, and a future where personalized treatments are the norm. But a major shortcoming has snagged that progress: CRISPR can make off-target edits to parts of the genome never meant to be touched.

science.title: Healthcare provider’s perceptions of digital antimicrobial stewardship in resource-limited settings
science.description: Antimicrobial resistance is a key public health concern globally, especially in resource-limited settings, where health system limitations contribute to poor antimicrobial stewardship. Digital health solutions present an opportunity to improve antimicrobial stewardship through better prescribing, surveillance, and clinical decision-making. Nevertheless, there is limited evidence on healthcare providers’ perceptions and contextual factors that affect the implementation of digital antimicrobial stewardship in low-resource settings. The objective of this study is to explore healthcare providers’ perceptions of digital antimicrobial stewardship in resource-limited primary hospitals. A descriptive qualitative study was conducted in public primary hospitals in the Wolaita Zone of Southern Ethiopia, utilizing in-depth interviews with purposively chosen healthcare providers. Data collection was done until thematic saturation was reached. The interviews were recorded on tape, transcribed verbatim, and analyzed through inductive thematic analysis using Opencode version 4.02 software. Fourteen participants were included in the study. Five key themes emerged: infrastructure-related issues, training and digital competency, organizational support and leadership, perceived usefulness of digital tools, and opportunities to enhance antimicrobial stewardship. Respondents identified the possibilities of digital tools to improve the accuracy of prescribing and monitoring; inappropriate digital infrastructure, insufficient training, and lack of institutional support were identified as barriers to successful implementation. The facilitators were leadership dedication, capacity-building efforts, and the incorporation of digital systems in daily clinical operations. Technological, human, and organizational factors are mutually dependent and influence the implementation of digital antimicrobial stewardship in resource-limited settings. Although healthcare providers have good perceptions about digital antimicrobial stewardship, there is a need to bridge the gap in infrastructure and capacity. Digital readiness and institutional support are needed to facilitate the successful implementation and sustainability of digital health interventions to fight antimicrobial resistance.
